The recommended bid stays comfortably inside cash and leaves the balance positive, which is the binding test - spending is capped by the floor rather than by cash, but a negative balance at matchday start scores ZERO for the entire matchday, so cash is the cap that actually matters. Hard rule for the next runs: do not add a second bid on top of this one. If both landed the balance would go negative and the whole matchday would score nothing.

binding_gap: Midfield, and specifically the zero. Amoako occupies a starting midfield slot with no points history whatsoever, so one eleventh of the fielded team is guaranteed to contribute nothing. With only one legal formation there is no way to shuffle him out - the squad has no twelfth body to replace him with. The Onyeka bid closes it and lifts the fielded average by about eleven percent; nothing else on the board does.

sell.reason: Nothing is sellable this run. Held back purely by the eleven-player floor, not by any judgement about the players. Once the buy lands the first sale is AMOAKO - and that is a deliberate change to the funding-sale order earlier runs set. Widmer, Bernardo and Lokonga were the designated sales, and all three are wrong to sell first, because all three sit in the best eleven and Amoako does not. With twelve players the best shape is still 5-3-2 and it drops Amoako anyway, so selling him leaves the fielded eleven completely untouched while banking his value. Selling Widmer instead would force Amoako back into the eleven and cost fielded points to raise a smaller sum. Amoako is also bleeding value fast with no performance floor under it, since he has never scored. His purchase premium was the third-highest in the whole measured log and the loss on him is sunk - not a reason to hold a player who produces nothing.

NOT URGENT relative to the buy: the buy has a 19:17Z deadline, this has until the 2026-09-04T18:30Z lock. Do it in that order and never the reverse.
